definition: Effrontery means shameless boldness; insolent nerve.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word effrontery. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know effrontery should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After crashing the wedding, eating two dinners, and leading the conga line, the stranger had the effrontery to complain about the band.
Boldness by itself can be a virtue — explorers need it; it stops well short of effrontery, which is nerve with the shame stripped out.
Impudence is cheeky disrespect — a smirk at the teacher; it stops short of effrontery, which is shamelessness on a grand scale.

Gall is the informal word for bitter, presumptuous nerve — 'the gall to ask for a refund after breaking it.' Effrontery is its formal cousin and goes further: shamelessness so complete the person seems not to feel embarrassment at all.

Audacity is boldness that can be admirable or shameless depending on the deed: an audacious business gamble can impress, an audacious lie disgusts. Effrontery cannot swing both ways — it is always disapproving, reserved for shamelessness that tramples what is owed to others.

Nerve is the everyday word for daring that oversteps — 'the nerve to show up uninvited' — though it can also be neutral grit, as when a climber keeps her nerve. Effrontery is never neutral: it is nerve with the shame removed, and always condemned.
